article.headline: Games To Watch: State-final spots await as Tupelo and Warren Central defend perfect runs
article.html:
Tupelo and Warren Central carry perfect football records into home games with state-championship berths on the line Friday night. Germantown visits the 13–0 Golden Wave, while South Panola travels to face the 12–0 Vikings. Both games kick off at 7 p.m. Central.

The remaining November 27, 2026, varsity slate also offers an unbeaten Benton team against Madison-Ridgeland Academy at the Lighthouse Classic, Olive Branch’s unbeaten girls at home, and a Horn Lake basketball doubleheader in Indianola. These are selected upcoming games, with entering records checked on their matchup pages. All times below are Central Standard Time.

Class 7A: Tupelo’s perfect run meets a winning road team

Germantown brings an 8–4 record to the 7 p.m. playoff game at Tupelo. The Mavericks’ current schedule also lists a four-game winning streak and a 5–2 away record. That makes the visitor’s recent form a meaningful part of this matchup: Tupelo is protecting a perfect season, while Germantown has been winning and has a successful road record of its own.

In the other 7A state-final qualifier, Brandon visits Oak Grove at 7 p.m. in Hattiesburg. Oak Grove enters 10–2 and Brandon 9–3. The class bracket places the winners of these two games opposite each other in the championship, so Friday’s results will settle both sides of that final. Earlier playoff coverage is available in our previous Friday varsity recap.

Class 6A: Warren Central defends a perfect record; Hattiesburg visits Picayune

South Panola is listed at 7–4 ahead of its 7 p.m. trip to Warren Central in Vicksburg. The Vikings have won all their reported games and now have a state-final place to secure at home. South Panola has reached the same stage with a different overall record, giving the Tigers a chance to end Warren Central’s unbeaten run while extending their own postseason.

The other 6A semifinal pairs Hattiesburg and host Picayune at 7 p.m., with both teams listed at 9–3. Their matching records give the Maroon Tide and Tigers an even comparison in wins and losses entering the game. The winner advances to meet either South Panola or Warren Central. The 6A bracket also lists viewing links for both semifinal matchups.

Class 5A: West Point and New Hope play for a championship berth

West Point visits New Hope at 7 p.m. in Columbus. The Green Wave are listed at 5–7 and the Trojans at 9–3, but both have reached the North-South round of the class bracket. That postseason position is the key to this game: New Hope can turn its home semifinal into a championship appearance, while West Point can advance despite an overall losing record. The 5A bracket includes a stream listing for the matchup.

Class 4A: Kosciusko–Louisville and Mendenhall–Poplarville set the final

Kosciusko enters the 7 p.m. game at Louisville at 12–1, with the Wildcats listed at 11–2. Both have double-digit wins and only a small number of defeats, making this one of the strongest record-based pairings in the selection. Their place in the North-South round adds the decisive stake: the winner moves into the state championship.

Poplarville hosts Mendenhall at 7 p.m. in the other 4A semifinal. The Hornets are 12–0 and the Tigers 11–2. Poplarville has a perfect season to protect against a visitor with a substantial winning record; the winner will face either Kosciusko or Louisville in the class final. The 4A bracket has the connected matchups and a viewing listing for Kosciusko–Louisville.

Winona puts a 13–0 record against Noxubee County

Winona is also unbeaten at 13–0 ahead of the 7 p.m. home game against Noxubee County. The visiting Tigers are listed at 11–2, and the matchup page explicitly identifies the game as the 3A North Half Championship. Winona’s perfect record and Noxubee County’s winning season therefore meet with a half-state title at stake.

Lighthouse Classic: MRA faces unbeaten Benton; Jackson Academy meets Kirkwood

Madison-Ridgeland Academy meets Benton at 4 p.m. in a neutral-site Lighthouse Classic game. Benton is 5–0 and MRA 4–1. The Patriots have a strong opening record and an opportunity to challenge a team without a reported loss. This is an early remaining tipoff in the selection, ahead of the evening football games.

Jackson Academy faces Kirkwood at 5:30 p.m. in the Lighthouse Classic in Corinth. The Raiders are 2–2 and Kirkwood, from Clarksville, Tennessee, is 3–0. Jackson Academy can move above an even record by handing the Cobras their first reported defeat. Both basketball games are listed as neutral-site matchups.

Olive Branch hosts Memphis East; Horn Lake travels to Gentry

Olive Branch’s girls bring a 3–0 record to the 5:30 p.m. home game against Memphis East. The visiting Mustangs are listed at 1–4. The Conquistadors have a perfect start to defend at home, while Memphis East has an opportunity to improve its opening against an unbeaten opponent.

Horn Lake’s girls are 6–2 ahead of their 6 p.m. game at Gentry in Indianola. The Rams enter 2–2. Horn Lake has a winning start to build on, while Gentry can move above an even record with a home victory.

The boys game follows at 7:30 p.m., with Horn Lake listed at 4–3 and Gentry at 4–2. Both teams have winning records entering the matchup, giving the later game a different balance from the girls opener. Our earlier basketball recap provides background on recent MRA and Horn Lake results.
